name: Grill and Skillet
summary: Quick heat and big flavour: chili-lime chicken, skillet salmon, beef kebabs, grilled vegetables and chickpeas, shrimp skewers and a tandoori-style tray. Every grilled dish has an indoor grill pan or broiler option, and the carbs are all whole foods.
howItWorks:
**Hot pan, big flavour.** Weeknight dinners take about 35 to 45 minutes: start the marinade first and prep the rest while it works. Chicken, beef, vegetables and shrimp go on a grill, grill pan or broiler, and the salmon and trout sear in a skillet. Marinades stay in the fridge and are never reused.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's chicken and corn salad, Wednesday's beef kebabs and quinoa, and Thursday's grilled vegetable plate each make two portions. The second is the next day's lunch, cooled within the hour and eaten within 3 days.

**Fish three times.** Skillet salmon on Tuesday, trout on Friday and a canned salmon bowl at the weekend bring **omega-3 and vitamin D**. Shrimp skewers add iodine, and beans, lentils, chickpeas or tofu turn up every day.

**Light.** It keeps one snack a day and trims the oats, quinoa, oil, nuts and potatoes first. At 1400 the chicken, beef and fish stay real portions, although Sunday's chicken is about two-thirds of its Standard size.

**Big.** The chicken, beef, salmon, trout, shrimp, beans, grains, potatoes, sweet potatoes, corn, oil and walnuts all grow, and Thursday gains a kiwi and walnut snack. Saturday's and Sunday's lunches swap places, and Sunday's apple snack becomes cherries, to keep each day balanced. The green and salad vegetables stay about as written.

recipes.name: Cherry and walnut overnight oats
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt, with frozen cherries that thaw into a ruby swirl, and a crunch of walnuts. Five minutes the night before gives you **protein and fibre** before the day starts.
steps: Wash your hands. Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until there are no dry patches.
Spoon the frozen cherries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. They thaw into the oats and turn them pink.
In the morning, stir it up. If it is too thick, loosen it with a splash of milk. Scatter the walnuts on just before eating so they stay crisp.
Keep the jar in the fridge and eat it within 2 days of making it.
recipes.tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen cherries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Toasted oat and quinoa porridge with skillet-seared banana
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a skillet-toasted oatmeal, with quinoa for a nutty bite
recipes.about: Oats and a little quinoa toasted in the pan, simmered in milk until creamy, then topped with banana slices seared until caramelised and crunchy sunflower seeds. The banana brings **potassium, and the seeds vitamin E**, so it needs no sugar.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve under cold water for 30 seconds. Warm a small saucepan over medium heat, add the oats and quinoa and toast them, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 2 minutes.

Pour in the milk and a splash of water, add the cinnamon and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 14 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a little more water if it gets thick, until the quinoa is tender and the porridge is creamy.
While it simmers, heat a dry nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and sear the banana slices for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden and caramelised.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the banana and sunflower seeds.
recipes.tip: Short on time? Use only rolled oats and simmer for 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Black bean, pepper and kale skillet scramble
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican huevos con frijoles
recipes.about: Eggs scrambled firm in a hot skillet with smoky black beans, sweet red pepper and a handful of kale, finished with feta. The beans and kale add **fibre, folate and iron**, so it fills you up without needing toast.
steps: Wash the pepper and kale. Warm the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the pepper and cook for 3 minutes until just soft.
Stir in the beans, cumin and paprika and cook for 2 minutes. Add the kale and a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until it wilts.
Crack the eggs in, add the salt and stir gently. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the eggs are completely set with no liquid and the yolks are firm.
Spoon onto a plate and crumble the feta over the top.
recipes.tip: A squeeze of lime at the end brightens it.

recipes.name: Chili-lime grilled chicken with charred corn and black bean salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican elote and a Tex-Mex grill supper
recipes.about: Chicken breast marinated in lime, chili and cumin, grilled until golden, on a bright salad of skillet-charred sweet corn, black beans, tomatoes and avocado. The beans and corn bring **fibre and folate**, the kale and carrot add calcium and vitamin A, and the lime on top helps you absorb the iron from the beans.

ingredients.note: kernels, thawed if frozen and patted dry

steps: Make the marinade in a shallow dish: half the lime juice, half the oil, the chili powder, paprika, cumin, garlic and half the salt. Trim any visible fat from the chicken, add it and turn to coat. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes or up to 4 hours. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan, or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element. Lift the chicken out, wipe off the extra marinade and discard it. Grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side, until golden with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits) and 74 °C (165 °F) on a thermometer in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes on a clean plate.
While the chicken cooks, heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the corn and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring only now and then, until the kernels are speckled golden at the edges.

Wash the tomatoes, kale, carrot, onion and cilantro. In a big bowl massage the kale with a pinch of the salt and a squeeze of the lime for a minute, then toss in the warm corn, beans, tomatoes, carrot, onion, cilantro, the rest of the lime juice, oil and salt.

Slice the chicken and serve it over the salad with the avocado, feta and sunflower seeds on top. Put the second portion in a shallow container, without the avocado, within 1 hour. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge; add fresh avocado at lunch. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
recipes.tip: Eat the leftover cold on the salad, or warm the chicken slices to 74 °C and keep the salad cold.

recipes.name: Skillet salmon with crisp garlic potatoes and asparagus
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a classic pan-seared salmon supper
recipes.about: Salmon seared skin-side down until the skin crackles, with golden garlicky potatoes and asparagus cooked in the same pan, finished with a lemon-parsley yogurt. The salmon brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the asparagus adds folate.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until nearly tender, then drain and let them steam dry for 2 minutes. Buy the salmon the day you cook it and keep it in the fridge until then.

Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes cut-side down with the paprika and cook for 8 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Add the garlic for the last minute so it does not burn. Move them to the side of the pan.

Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Add the rest of the oil to the free half of the pan and lay the salmon in skin-side down. Cook for 5 minutes until the skin is crisp, flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until it flakes and reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part.
Add the asparagus to the pan for the last 3 minutes, turning, until bright green and just tender. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw fish.

Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice and half the parsley and a pinch of salt. Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the salmon, potatoes and asparagus, spoon the yogurt alongside and scatter with the rest of the parsley.
recipes.tip: Salmon is cooked fresh and not saved for later; eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Lean beef kebabs with herby quinoa and cucumber-tomato salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern shish kebab and tabbouleh, with quinoa for the grain
recipes.about: Cubes of lean sirloin and red pepper marinated in lemon, garlic and cumin, grilled on skewers and served on a lemony quinoa salad packed with parsley and mint. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, and the lemon and parsley help you absorb the iron in the quinoa.

ingredients.note: trimmed of all visible fat, cut in 3 cm cubes

steps: If you use wooden skewers, put them in water to soak for 30 minutes before you start. Mix half the lemon juice, half the oil, the garlic, cumin, paprika and a pinch of the salt in a dish. Trim any visible fat from the beef, add the cubes, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 20 minutes and up to 4 hours. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after handling the raw beef.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until the germ ring pops out. Drain well, spread it on a tray to cool, and fluff it with a fork.

Thread the beef, pepper and onion onto skewers. Grill over medium-high heat, or in a grill pan, or under a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element, for 8 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned with a few dark grill marks. Push the thermometer in from the side into the centre of the largest cube: it should read 71 °C (160 °F). Rest for 3 minutes on a clean plate.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the parsley, mint, cucumber, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and oil and the walnuts.

Serve the kebabs on the quinoa. Put the second portion in a shallow container in the fridge within 1 hour, and keep it up to 3 days. Reheat the beef to 74 °C (165 °F) and eat the quinoa salad cold. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
recipes.tip: Cut the beef into cubes of the same size so they all cook at once.

recipes.name: Grilled vegetable plate with crisp chickpeas and garlic-yogurt sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine mezze, eaten as a main
recipes.about: Asparagus, carrot, red pepper and onion grilled until tender and golden, with chickpeas crisped in the skillet and a cool garlic-mint yogurt sauce. Chickpeas, feta and walnuts make it a **proper, protein-rich meal**, and the carrots bring vitamin A.
steps: Put the carrot halves in a bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave for 3 minutes (or simmer them for 4 minutes) until they start to soften, then pat dry. Brush all the vegetables with half the oil and sprinkle with half the salt. Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element.

Grill the vegetables in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until tender with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits). Start the carrot and onion first, then the pepper and asparagus.

While the vegetables cook, heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chickpeas with the cumin and paprika and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and a little crisp.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice, mint and a pinch of salt.

Pile the vegetables on a plate, spoon over the chickpeas and the sauce, and finish with the feta and walnuts. Put the second portion in a shallow container, sauce on the side, within 1 hour. Keep up to 3 days and eat it cold or at room temperature. If you pack it for lunch, carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.
recipes.tip: Eat the leftover cold with the sauce spooned on, or warm only the chickpeas to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Smoky skillet trout with sweet potato wedges, blistered tomatoes and avocado-lime yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Southern-style pan-fried fish supper, with a Tex-Mex avocado crema
recipes.about: Trout fillets rubbed with smoked paprika and cumin, seared until crisp, with roasted sweet potato wedges, cherry tomatoes blistered in the same pan and a cool avocado-lime yogurt. The trout brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the sweet potato and tomatoes bring vitamin A and C.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the sweet potato wedges with a third of the oil, half the paprika and half the salt on a tray. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges.
Mash the avocado with the yogurt, lime juice, garlic and a pinch of salt until creamy, then stir in half the cilantro. Buy the trout the day you cook it and keep it in the fridge until then.

Pat the trout dry and rub the flesh with the cumin, the rest of the paprika and a little oil. Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the trout skin-side down for 4 minutes until crisp, flip and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it flakes and reads 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part. Wash your hands, the board and the plate that held the raw fish.
Lift the trout onto a clean plate. Add the whole tomatoes to the hot pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking, until they blister and just burst.
Serve the trout with the wedges and tomatoes, spoon over the avocado-lime yogurt and scatter with the rest of the cilantro.
recipes.tip: Salmon works in place of the trout.

recipes.name: Lemon-garlic shrimp skewers with warm lentil and herb salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mediterranean grilled prawns on a warm lentil salad
recipes.about: Shrimp tossed in lemon, garlic and smoked paprika, grilled in minutes, on a warm lentil salad with softened red pepper, red onion, parsley and mint. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the shrimp bring iodine.

ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, thawed in the fridge if frozen

steps: If you use wooden skewers, put them in water to soak for 30 minutes before you start. Mix half the lemon juice, the garlic, paprika, chili flakes, half the oil and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the shrimp, toss and marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the bowl and the board after handling the raw shrimp.

Warm the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the pepper and onion for 4 minutes, add the lentils and warm them through for 3 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in the rest of the lemon juice, the parsley, mint, cucumber and a pinch of salt.

Thread the shrimp onto the skewers. Lift them from the marinade and discard it. Grill over high heat, or in a grill pan, or under a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element, for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque, lightly browned (never black) and 70 °C (158 °F) in the thickest part.
Spoon the lentil salad onto a plate, lay the skewers on top and scatter with the walnuts.
recipes.tip: Cook shrimp the day you thaw them and do not save them.

recipes.name: Tandoori-style grilled chicken with spiced sweet potato, chickpeas and cucumber raita
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian tandoori chicken, cooked on a grill or broiler instead of in a clay oven
recipes.about: Chicken breast marinated in yogurt, ginger, garlic and garam masala, grilled until golden, with a tray of cumin-roasted sweet potato and chickpeas and a cooling cucumber raita. The yogurt marinade keeps the lean breast tender, and the sweet potato brings **vitamin A and potassium**.

ingredients.note: half for the marinade, half for the raita

steps: Stir half the yogurt with the ginger, garlic, garam masala, turmeric, lemon juice and half the salt in a dish. Trim any visible fat from the chicken, add it, turn to coat, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour and up to overnight. Never reuse the marinade. Wash your hands, the knife and the board with hot soapy water after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the sweet potato and chickpeas with half the oil, the cumin and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the sweet potato is tender and browned at the edges.

Heat the grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan, or a broiler with the rack about 10 cm from the element. Lift the chicken out of the marinade, wipe off the extra and discard it. Brush with the rest of the oil and grill for 6 to 7 minutes per side, until golden with a few dark grill marks (never black; trim off any black bits) and 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part. Rest for 5 minutes on a clean plate.
Wash the cucumber and mint. Stir the grated cucumber (squeezed dry), the rest of the yogurt, the mint and a pinch of salt into a raita.
Slice the chicken and serve with the sweet potato, chickpeas and raita.
recipes.tip: Marinate in the morning for the best flavour. If your broiler is in the same oven, roast the tray first and keep it warm while the chicken cooks. Cook only what you will eat that day.

recipes.name: Garlicky lentil and tomato skillet with firm-set eggs
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern lentils with tomato and eggs
recipes.about: Lentils simmered with garlic, tomato and smoked paprika with eggs set firm on top, all in one skillet. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lemon at the end helps you absorb the iron.
steps: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic, paprika, cumin and chili flakes and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 5 minutes until they collapse into a sauce. Stir in the lentils and 3 tablespoons of water and simmer for 3 minutes.
Make a well in the lentils for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm all the way through.
Finish with the lemon juice, parsley and feta.
recipes.tip: Eat it straight away; eggs are not saved for later.

recipes.name: Skillet buckwheat with crisp tofu, red pepper and kale
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a ginger-sesame tofu stir-fry, over buckwheat groats
recipes.about: Nutty buckwheat groats under golden tofu, red pepper and kale tossed in ginger and garlic, with a lime-tahini drizzle. It is a **meat-free, protein-rich** lunch, with magnesium from the buckwheat and some calcium from the calcium-set tofu.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, then simmer it in twice its volume of water with a pinch of salt for 12 minutes, until tender and the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the pepper and cook for 4 minutes until soft and a little browned. Add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then the kale, a splash of water and the salt and toss for 2 minutes until the kale wilts.
Whisk the tahini with the lime juice and 1 tablespoon of water. Return the tofu to the pan, spoon everything over the buckwheat, drizzle with the tahini and top with the grated carrot.
recipes.tip: To pack it, make it the evening before: cool it in a shallow container within 1 hour, keep it in the fridge and carry it in a cold bag with an ice pack. Eat it cold or warmed to 74 °C.

recipes.name: Smoky black bean and sweet potato skillet with red pepper and avocado
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Tex-Mex bean and sweet potato taco filling, without the tortilla
recipes.about: Diced sweet potato browned in a skillet with cumin and smoked paprika, then black beans and red pepper, with creamy avocado and feta on top. The sweet potato brings **vitamin A**, and the beans bring fibre, folate and plant protein.
steps: Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and a splash of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once, until nearly tender. Uncover and cook for 4 minutes more until browned at the edges.
Add the pepper, onion, cumin, paprika, chili powder and salt and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the beans and cook for 3 minutes until hot.
Finish with the lime juice. Top with the avocado, feta and cilantro.

recipes.name: Canned salmon bowl with charred corn, seared broccoli and lemon-tahini
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a Mediterranean-style salad bowl, with skillet-charred corn
recipes.about: Flaked canned salmon on skillet-charred sweet corn with broccoli seared in a hot skillet until tender and a little browned, crunchy cucumber and carrot and a lemon-tahini sauce. The salmon, with its soft bones, brings **omega-3, calcium and vitamin D**.

ingredients.note: kernels, thawed if frozen and patted dry

steps: Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the corn and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring only now and then, until the kernels are speckled golden at the edges. Tip it onto a plate.
Add the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and sear for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until bright green with golden edges.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, 1 tablespoon of water and the salt into a smooth sauce.
Fill a bowl with the corn, broccoli, cucumber, carrot, onion and parsley. Flake the salmon on top and drizzle with the sauce.
Keep any opened tin of fish covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. If you pack this, use a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day.

recipes.name: Orange with walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a handful of walnuts. The orange gives **vitamin C** and the walnuts plant omega-3 and crunch.
steps: Wash the orange before peeling it, then peel and segment it. Eat it with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Kiwi with walnuts
recipes.about: Sweet-tart kiwi with crunchy walnuts. Together they bring **vitamin C and plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the kiwi, slice it in half and scoop with a spoon. Eat with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Carrot and pepper sticks with lemon-tahini dip
recipes.about: Crunchy carrot and red pepper sticks for dunking in a creamy lemon-tahini dip. A snack with **vitamin A, vitamin C and some calcium**.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks. Stir the tahini, lemon juice, salt and about 1 tablespoon of water into a smooth dip and serve it alongside.

recipes.name: Skillet-toasted spiced chickpeas
recipes.about: Chickpeas crisped in a hot skillet with cumin and smoked paprika. Crunchy, savoury and full of **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chickpeas and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and crisp. Toss with the cumin, paprika and salt and let them cool for a few minutes before eating.

recipes.name: Skillet-charred edamame with lime and chili
recipes.about: Edamame charred in a hot dry skillet with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of chili. A snack with **plant protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Heat a dry skillet over high heat. Add the frozen edamame and a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes, then uncover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing, until the water is gone, they are hot all the way through and blistered in spots. Toss with the lime juice, chili flakes and salt and let them cool for a minute.

recipes.name: Skillet-warmed cinnamon apple with tahini
recipes.about: Apple slices warmed in a skillet until just soft, with a swirl of tahini. Sweet, nutty and filling, with **fibre and a little calcium**.
steps: Wash and slice the apple. Warm a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the apple and the cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until just soft and golden at the edges. Drizzle with the tahini.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with kiwi and walnuts
recipes.about: Thick yogurt with chopped kiwi and crunchy walnuts. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin C**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, add the chopped kiwi and scatter with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Cherries with walnuts
recipes.about: Sweet cherries with crunchy walnuts. It brings **vitamin C and plant omega-3**.
steps: Thaw the cherries in the fridge, then drain any extra juice and eat them with the walnuts.
recipes.tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, simmer the frozen cherries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana with walnuts and a shake of cinnamon. It brings **potassium and plant omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana, scatter with the walnuts and cinnamon.
